conflicts.about: Whether genus and species are asked for every kind of goods, or only for plants for planting

positions.says: Read literally, category and genus are asked for all goods and species only for plants for planting.
The line's punctuation does not say whether '(for plants for planting)' covers species alone or genus and species together.
IPAFFS asks for a genus-and-species pick from reference data for every plant commodity, and will not continue until at least one is added.
Continuing with no species added shows 'Select at least one species'.

conflicts.outcome: Precedence cannot settle it: the higher source is ambiguous on its own terms, not in disagreement with the trace. Built to the default until answered.
conflicts.question: Does the importer give genus and species for every commodity line, or genus for every line and species only for plants for planting?
conflicts.default: Every commodity line needs one genus-and-species pick from the reference data, whatever the category. This satisfies both readings of the policy, since asking more is safe and asking less is not, and it matches IPAFFS.

conflicts.about: What the categories of goods are

positions.says: The category is asked for, with 'plants for planting' and 'cut wood' given only as examples ('e.g.'), so the full list is not stated.

conflicts.outcome: A gap that matters: the category drives which other questions apply. The trace slice has no category question to compare against.
conflicts.question: What is the full list of goods categories the importer chooses from?
conflicts.default: Four categories, taken from the kinds of goods the policy page itself names: plants for planting; cut trees; wood and wood products (including isolated bark); other plants and plant products. One category per commodity line, required.

conflicts.about: What quantity is measured, and in what unit

positions.says: Quantity is 'of the relevant goods, as detailed in paragraph 1', but paragraph 1 is not on the page, so what is counted and in what unit is not stated.

conflicts.outcome: A gap that matters: the answer shapes the field. The trace slice does not cover quantity.
conflicts.question: What does the quantity count for each commodity line, and in which units?
conflicts.default: Each commodity line records one quantity: a whole number greater than zero and a unit chosen from a short fixed list (number of items, kilograms). Required on every line.

conflicts.about: Whether the importer gives a variety and class for each genus and species

positions.says: The policy's data list for all other goods names category, genus, species, commodity code, quantity and other items, but no variety and no class.
IPAFFS shows a Variety and class page, with a Variety select and a Class select (Class I, Class II, Extra Class), for any species whose reference data carries both.

conflicts.outcome: Policy wins. Variety and class are not in the policy's data list, so they are not adopted. The IPAFFS page, its 'Other' variety box, its validation and the class branch in the page order are all out of scope.

conflicts.about: Whether a UK region is recorded alongside the country of origin

positions.says: The notification gives 'the country from which the plants or wood originate' and nothing finer.
Choosing England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland also records a separate, optional region of origin.

conflicts.outcome: Policy wins. The notification records a country only; no region of origin is captured.

conflicts.about: The error message wording for a missing country of origin or a missing genus and species

positions.says: The IPAFFS frontend says 'Select the country of origin of plants, plant product or other objects'.
A second, backend layer says only 'Country of origin'.
Frontend and backend word the same required-field errors differently ('Enter/Select the …' against 'Add the …') and the trace set left it unresolved.
No error state on these pages was ever seen rendered; all error copy is transcribed from source code.

conflicts.outcome: Both sides are the same source at the same tier, and the policy is silent, so precedence cannot settle it. Built to the default until answered.
conflicts.question: Which error wording should a missing country of origin and a missing genus and species show?
conflicts.default: The IPAFFS frontend wording, in GOV.UK 'Select …' style: 'Select the country of origin of plants, plant product or other objects' and 'Select at least one species'. One message per error, shown in the error summary and beside the field.

conflicts.about: Whether the policy's published data list is still current

positions.says: The list is 'True at time of publishing'; readers should contact two named policy leads for an up-to-date list.

conflicts.outcome: A gap that matters: the whole programme builds to this list. Nothing blocks on it.
conflicts.question: Have the policy leads confirmed that the 'All other goods' data list on the Requirements catalogue page is still current?
conflicts.default: Build to the list as published on the page. Any later change becomes a new requirement.
